title: Oligopolistic Behaviour of Major Oil Companies and Realistic Petrol Pump Prices in Singapore
what_it_is: Oligopolistic Behaviour of Major Oil Companies and Realistic Petrol Pump Prices in Singapore

sections.label: Questions on oil companies oligopoly
sections.summary: An MP asked whether oil companies behave as an oligopoly, the realistic Octane 95 price at zero crude price, and whether lowest prices must be published.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether there are indications that the major oil companies in Singapore behave like an oligopoly; (b) what is the realistic selling price of the popular Octane 95 petrol when the crude oil price is zero or less; and (c) whether the Ministry will mandate oil companies to publish their lowest petrol and diesel prices after their best discounts.

sections.label: Brent Crude price fall
sections.summary: Brent Crude fell from US$28 per barrel on 20 April to US$16 on 22 April, the lowest in over two decades.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Brent Crude fell from US$28 per barrel at the start of 20 April to a low of US$16 a barrel on 22 April, the lowest price in over two decades.

sections.label: 2017 CCS petrol cost study
sections.summary: A 2017 study by then-CCS found refined petrol costs were less than one-third of the listed retail petrol price.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The detailed study published by then-Competition Commission of Singapore (CCS) in 2017 found that refined petrol costs accounted for less than one-third of the listed retail petrol price.

sections.label: Petrol retailers price monitoring
sections.summary: The 2017 study found major petrol retailers monitor and respond to each other's prices and promotions, though prices do not always move in tandem; CCCS monitors and will enforce against anti-competitive activity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The 2017 study found that the major petrol retailers do regularly monitor and respond to each other's prices and promotions, but also found that prices do not always move in tandem among the petrol retailers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: The Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCCS) is monitoring closely and will take enforcement action should evidence of anti-competitive activity surface.

sections.label: MOPS and retail petrol prices
sections.summary: The 2017 report found listed retail petrol prices changed an average of seven cents per ten-cent MOPS change, with adjustments over eight days for increases and six for decreases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: The 2017 report by then-CCS found that between January 2010 and December 2016, for every 10 cents change in Mean of Platts (MOPS) price, the listed retail petrol price changed by an average of seven cents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: On average, adjustments in listed retail petrol price, took place over eight days for MOPS' price increases and six days for MOPS' price decreases.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: In 2015, MOPS made up less than one-third of total listed petrol price and the non fuel components such as operating costs, taxes, duties, land costs, discounts and rebates made up the remaining amount.

sections.label: Fuel stocks retail restriction
sections.summary: Companies keeping such fuel stocks for their own vehicles are currently not allowed to retail to the public.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: At the moment, companies maintaining such fuel stocks for their own vehicles are not allowed to retail to the public.

sections.label: Fuel Kaki website development
sections.summary: A 2017 study found consumers lacked access to and awareness of retail petrol prices, so MTI and CCCS worked with CASE to develop the Fuel Kaki website.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: The 2017 study by the then-CCS had found that there was a lack of ready access to, and awareness of, retail petrol prices by consumers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: Following that study, MTI and CCCS worked with CASE to develop the Fuel Kaki website to help improve transparency for petrol prices.

sections.label: Fuel Kaki Price Estimator
sections.summary: Fuel Kaki has a Price Estimator that lets individual consumers find which petrol retailer offers the lowest effective price based on their eligibility for discounts and rebates.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: But it also has a Price Estimator within.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: And as individual consumers, you can find out which petrol retailer offers the lowest effective price based on your individual eligibility for discounts and rebates.

sections.label: Fuel Kaki empowers consumers
sections.summary: Fuel Kaki helps journalists and analysts and, by making effective price comparison easier, empowers consumers, who deter unreasonable pricing; work with CASE will continue.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: If you are a journalist or an analyst, it helps you, too.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: So, by making it easier for consumers to compare effective prices, Fuel Kaki helps empower consumers and, as mentioned earlier, well-informed consumers are a key deterrent against unreasonable pricing and we will continue to work with CASE to improve Fuel Kaki and to continue empowering all our consumers.
